messages.content: Get the protein sequence of human HbA1c, normal hemoglobin, and rat hemoglobin and their 3D models

function.name: protein_info_get_sequence_and_3D
function.description: Retrive the sequence and 3D models of proteins. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

model_3d.description: Set true to get 3D model of the protein.

message.reasoning: We need to retrieve protein sequences and 3D models for human HbA1c (glycated hemoglobin), normal hemoglobin (human?), and rat hemoglobin. Use the function protein_info_get_sequence_and_3D. Provide protein_name. For HbA1c, maybe "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" or "Hemoglobin subunit beta"? But HbA1c refers to glycated hemoglobin, which is the same as normal hemoglobin but with glucose attached. Sequence is same as normal hemoglobin. So we can provide "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" and "Hemoglobin subunit beta" for human. For rat hemoglobin, similar subunits. But the user likely wants the entire hemoglobin protein? Usually hemoglobin is heterodimer of alpha and beta chains. We can provide both chains. Provide 3D models. Use function twice? We can call function for each protein. Provide name like "Human Hemoglobin subunit alpha", "Human Hemoglobin subunit beta", "Rat Hemoglobin subunit alpha", "Rat Hemoglobin subunit beta". For HbA1c, maybe "Human Hemoglobin subunit alpha (glycated)"? But sequence same. We can just note that sequence same as normal. Provide 3D model of hemoglobin (PDB). Use function with model_3d true. Let's call function for each.
